plot: Odo and Mothwick follow the true story of the Gloucester sea serpent (Massachusetts, August 1817): hundreds of townspeople see a 60-foot humped creature in daylight, a gunshot fails, and Boston scientists name a new species from a small bumpy snake — the twist is that the snake was just a deformed black snake, but nobody has explained what the crowds saw, and the water starts moving with no wind.

script.title: Hundreds Saw It. Would You Swim Here?

beats.say: There! In the harbor! Something long is coming straight at us!
A true story. Gloucester, Massachusetts, August eighteen seventeen. Broad daylight.
Hundreds of people saw it. So why could nobody ever catch it?
New episode every day — subscribe so you don't miss what happens next.
Fairies by a stream... and now something in the sea?
Whatever watched your lantern ran toward the water, Odo.
Gloucester was a fishing town. Its people knew the sea well.
But for days that August, crowds gathered on the shore to stare.
A Boston newspaper said hundreds watched it over several days.
Sixty feet long, at least! And as thick as a barrel!
Witnesses said its head looked like a turtle's, but far bigger.
Its back rose in humps, like buoys strung along a net.
It was fast. It could double back on itself in an instant.
Something that big... and nobody could catch it?
On August fourteenth, men rowed out to it with a gun.
Steady... steady... now! Fire!
The creature sank. Then it rose again, a hundred yards away.
A gunshot couldn't stop it. So what on earth was it?
A ship's captain, Solomon Allen, put his sighting into words.
A strange marine animal. I believe it to be a serpent.
In Boston, the Linnaean Society sent a committee to find out more.
Every witness, one at a time. We will write it all down.
One member, John Davis, warned that the stories did not agree.
It was seen badly, he said, and always moving fast.
In late September, a farmer killed a strange snake by the shore.
Three feet long, and look! Its whole back is bumpy!
Humps! Just like the serpent. This must be its young!
The society named a brand new species. Scoliophis atlanticus.
So they found it! The mystery is solved!
If that little snake is wrong, the whole report looks foolish.
Many laughed at the report. A playwright even mocked it on stage.
Decades later, Boston scientists looked at that little snake again.
It was a common black snake. Its spine was simply deformed.
So the scientists' great proof was just an ordinary snake?
The famous baby serpent had never been a serpent at all.
So what did hundreds of people see? Many now suggest a whale.
A feeding humpback, rolling at the surface, can look like humps.
A whale that doubles back on itself in an instant?
A whale that stayed in one harbor for days, before crowds?
The sightings went on. Nahant in eighteen nineteen, then for a century.
The last reports of a serpent off Gloucester came in nineteen sixty.
Since then, nothing. The harbor has stayed quiet.
Mothwick... the water is moving. But there's no wind.
Next time: the day New England's sun went out at noon.
What do you think happens in the next part? Tell me in the comments.

long.description:
What do you think happens in the next part? Tell me in the comments.

"A whole town saw it in daylight. And still nobody could say what it was." — Odo

A true story from Gloucester, Massachusetts: in August 1817 hundreds of people watched a huge humped serpent in their harbor. A gunshot failed, scientists named a new species — and then their proof fell apart.
